instruction: Add nancy@someuniversity.edu and stella@someuniversity.edu to the email's To field.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened tuition_payment.xlsx, misread 2 of 4 unpaid students (typed john and sophia instead of iron and stella), added emails to To field, then spent remaining turns stuck on network save dialog.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open files from file manager, read spreadsheet data, switch between windows, type email addresses into Thunderbird compose To field, interact with Thunderbird dialogs.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model hallucinated spreadsheet data - correctly identified fox and nancy as unpaid but incorrectly added john and sophia (who had 'Yes') instead of iron and stella. Then wasted ~20 turns waiting for stuck network save.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests adding two email addresses directly (no spreadsheet reading). Addresses are given explicitly in the instruction to isolate the Thunderbird interaction capability from data lookup.
metadata.explanation: Task requires adding two email addresses to the Thunderbird compose To field. Evaluator checks accessibility tree for address pills containing nancy@ and stella@someuniversity.edu. Partial credit: 0.5 per email.

scoring_breakdown.add_nancy_email: 0.5 - nancy@someuniversity.edu appears as address pill in To field
scoring_breakdown.add_stella_email: 0.5 - stella@someuniversity.edu appears as address pill in To field

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses accessibility tree CSS selectors to verify both email addresses (nancy@someuniversity.edu and stella@someuniversity.edu) appear as address pills in the Thunderbird compose To field.
Complete coverage: both required emails from the instruction are checked by separate rules.

CSS selectors correctly target MsgHeadersToolbar > To label siblings with class 'address-pill' > pill-label containing the email, which matches Thunderbird's compose window accessibility tree structure.
Postconfig includes a 10-second sleep to allow Thunderbird UI to settle before reading the accessibility tree.

Minor issue: metadata claims partial credit (0.5 per email) but check_accessibility_tree returns 0 immediately if any rule fails — no actual partial credit. The evaluator is stricter than documented but still correctly verifies task completion.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To support the claimed partial credit scoring, consider using separate evaluator entries (one per email) or modifying the evaluation approach so each email contributes 0.5 independently. Currently check_accessibility_tree returns 0 if any rule has no matching elements.
